bull.t: Roche partnership strengthens funding and commercialization
bull.b: The Roche alliance provides substantial non-dilutive funding potential, shared development economics and global commercialization capabilities. Roche’s infrastructure may accelerate clinical development and expand access to markets that Nurix could not efficiently address alone.

bull.t: Bexobrutideg shows strong clinical activity and tolerability
bull.b: High response rates in difficult-to-treat and earlier-line populations, combined with no dose-limiting toxicities reported, support the asset’s differentiation. Durable efficacy could underpin late-stage development and broaden Nurix’s oncology opportunity.

Modest debt relative to equity and a sizable asset base reduce immediate balance-sheet pressure. This gives Nurix more flexibility to fund research, absorb development setbacks and use partnership proceeds without relying entirely on additional debt.

bear.t: Revenue contraction and widening losses weaken financial performance
bear.b: The sharp revenue decline and expanding net loss show that collaboration income is not yet translating into stable operating performance. Persistent negative results reduce earnings visibility and increase reliance on successful pipeline advancement and future funding.

bear.t: Persistent cash burn creates funding risk
bear.b: Large recurring cash outflows reflect the cost of advancing a broad clinical pipeline without commercial product revenue. Even with partnership funding, sustained burn could require additional financing if milestones, approvals or operating improvements are delayed.

bear.t: Clinical-stage model lacks commercial product revenue
bear.b: Nurix has no established commercial product base to provide recurring sales or diversify development risk. Its financial profile therefore depends heavily on partnerships, milestones and eventual approvals, making pipeline setbacks especially consequential.
